title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Maya Kapoor
body:
Purpose:
This document centralizes Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard processes for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the single reference for employees, managers, and approvers to ensure consistent, secure, and auditable operations across the company.

Scope:
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party services that interact with Redwood systems, data, or purchasing processes. Specific teams may have additional requirements (see related pages).

1) Access and Permissions
Overview:
Access to systems follows the principle of least privilege with role-based access control (RBAC). All access requests must be authorized, time-bounded when appropriate, and reviewed periodically.

Key Roles and Responsibilities:
- People Ops: ownership of account provisioning for corporate systems (G Suite, HRIS, Okta) and onboarding/offboarding checklist.
- Security: owner of privileged access reviews, SSO/KMS configuration, and emergency access processes.
- Team Managers: validate role requirements and approve access in GitHub, Slack, Jira, Confluence, and internal services.

Onboarding / Offboarding Checklist (high-level):
1. People Ops creates user in IdP (Okta) and assigns baseline groups.
2. Manager submits specific role access requests via the Access Request form (link in Templates).
3. Security reviews privileged access requests (admins, cloud infra, KMS) within 48 hours.
4. On offboard, People Ops initiates account deactivation, communicates to SRE/Infra for credential rotation, and triggers device wipe if applicable.

Access Request and Approval Matrix (summary table):
| Resource Type | Requester | Approver | Security Review Required | Expiry default |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Non-sensitive SaaS (e.g., marketing tools) | Team manager | Team manager | No | 12 months |
| Code repo (read) | Team manager | Repo owner | No | 12 months |
| Code repo (write/admin) | Team manager | Repo owner + Security | Yes (privileged) | 6 months |
| Production infra (read) | Team manager | Infra owner | Yes | 3 months |
| Production infra (admin) | Security | Security lead + Exec | Yes + MFA | 30 days (just-in-time) |

Periodic Reviews:
- Managers must review team members' access quarterly.
- Security performs company-wide privileged access audit every 6 months.

Emergency Access (Break-glass):
- Process: Submit emergency access request via PagerDuty incident or Security Slack channel with justification. Security triages and grants time-limited access (max 4 hours) and logs the session. Post-incident review required within 72 hours.

2) Change Management
Goal:
Ensure safe, observable, and auditable changes to production and critical systems while minimizing risk to customers and internal continuity.

Change Categories:
- Standard changes: low-risk, pre-approved (routine cronjob updates, minor config updates)
- Normal changes: require change ticket, peer review, and scheduled maintenance window
- Emergency changes: unplanned, necessary to restore service or mitigate active incident

Process (Normal changes):
1. Create change ticket in Jira with: owner, impact assessment, rollback plan, test plan, monitoring/alerting adjustments, and scheduled window.
2. Peer review by at least one engineer not on the delivery team.
3. Approver sign-off: Service owner + Release Engineering.
4. Implement in a staging environment; run acceptance tests.
5. Execute during approved window; monitor for predefined KPIs for at least 2x the expected effect time.
6. Post-change verification and close ticket with summary and links to telemetry.

Emergency change controls:
- Must be documented in Jira post-hoc with timeline, the reason for bypassing normal approvals, and a postmortem if customer-visible.

Change windows and maintenances:
- Non-critical maintenance: weekdays 10:00-18:00 local PT.
- Critical maintenance: schedule with Product and Customer Success 7+ days in advance.

3) Data Management
Principles:
- Classify: All data is classified as Public, Internal, or Restricted. Sensitive customer data and PII must be treated as Restricted.
- Minimize: Store the minimum data necessary.
- Protect: Use encryption (at-rest and in-transit), access controls, and logging.

Data Ownership and Inventory:
- Data owners (product or platform teams) must maintain a simple inventory for datasets they own: purpose, classification, retention period, and location.
- The Security team maintains a central inventory of all Restricted datasets and coordinates periodic reviews.

Retention and Deletion:
- Default retention: Internal logs 90 days, Customer analytics 365 days, Restricted datasets per contractual/legal requirement (specified in contracts).
- Deletion requests: follow the Data Deletion Request form and are executed within defined SLA (30 days for non-legal requests).

Backups and Restore:
- Critical systems: daily backups, weekly snapshot verification, annual restore test.
- Backup encryption and access restricted to backup administrators.

Data Access for Research / Model Training:
- All datasets used for model training must be approved by Data Owner and Security; a Data Use Agreement (DUA) is required for third-party datasets.
- Anonymization or tokenization must be applied when feasible.

4) Procurement and Expenses
Policy Objectives:
- Ensure spending aligns with company budget and procurement controls. Provide clear approval paths and documentation for audits.

Purchase categories and approval limits:
- <$1,000: Manager-level approval (expense report allowed)
- $1,000- $10,000: Department head approval + Finance notification
- >$10,000: Finance + Procurement + Exec sponsor approval

Procurement process (step-by-step):
1. Submit purchase request in Procurement Portal with justification, budget code, and preferred vendor.
2. Procurement reviews for vendor compliance, contract needs, and TCO.
3. Finance verifies budget and issues P-card or PO.
4. Receive goods/services and submit invoice to AP with matching PO and receipt.

Expense reporting:
- Employees must upload receipts within 30 days. Cardholder reconciliations due monthly. Non-compliant expenses may be denied.

Travel booking and per-diem (summary):
- Use designated travel portal for airfare/hotels. Economy or equivalent for domestic travel, premium economy or business for long-haul >8 hours with Manager pre-approval. Meal per-diems by region (link to internal spreadsheet template).

5) Vendor Management
Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Business owner identifies need and completes Vendor Intake form.
2. Procurement performs Sourcing and Security review (including SOC2/ISO evidence if required).
3. Legal completes contract review and approves terms; Finance sets payment terms.
4. Security configures network segmentation, least-privilege integration, and monitoring if vendor integrates with production systems.

Vendor Risk Tiers and Controls (summary):
- Tier 1 (High): vendors with access to production or Restricted data. Controls: contract with security clauses, quarterly reviews, SOC2/ISO evidence, annual penetration test where relevant.
- Tier 2 (Medium): vendors with internal data access or critical services. Controls: annual attestation, quarterly incident notification clause.
- Tier 3 (Low): marketing tools, one-off consultants. Controls: standard contract, annual procurement review.

Offboarding vendors:
- Revoke credentials and API keys, remove network access, confirm invoice closure, and archive contracts for 7 years.

6) Travel Policy (detailed highlights)
- Safety-first: Employees traveling on company business must register trips in the Travel Portal and share itinerary with manager.
- Approvals: All travel requires Manager pre-approval. International travel also requires People Ops notification for visa and insurance assistance.
- Reimbursable expenses: airfare, lodging, ground transport, per-diem meals, reasonable business phone/data charges.
- Non-reimbursable: spouse/partner travel, leisure upgrades without manager approval, personal purchases.

Incident and Insurance:
- Company travel insurance covers medical evacuation for business trips registered in the Travel Portal. Unregistered travel may not be covered.

7) Internal Templates and Forms
Included templates (links to copy in Templates space):
- Access Request form (SaaS and infra variants)
- Vendor Intake and Vendor Risk Assessment templates
- Purchase Request and PO template
- Travel authorization and expense report template
- Data Deletion Request form and Data Use Agreement (DUA) template
- Change ticket checklist and post-change verification checklist

How to use templates:
- Always make a copy of the canonical template (do not edit the master). Populate required fields and attach supporting documents. Templates have built-in fields that drive downstream automation (Procurement Portal, Access Request tracker).

Governance, Exceptions, and Escalation
- Exceptions: Any exception to these policies must be requested via the Exception Request form and approved by People Ops and the policy owner (Security or Finance as applicable).
- Escalation: For disputes or policy interpretation, escalate to the policy owner. For unresolved issues, route to the CTO/Head of People Ops for final determination.

Audit and Compliance
- Finance, Security, and People Ops will perform annual audits of procurement, privileged access, and vendor contracts.
- All records (contracts, vendor evidence, purchase orders) must be retained for a minimum of 7 years unless legal requires otherwise.
